messages:
olivia: Heads-up — saw a small cluster of client reconnects midstream at ~10:02 UTC. Console traces point to keepalive coalescing on the proxy layer causing delayed ping delivery and the backends closing streams with 408/EOF.

kai: hmm — coalescing? we intentionally batch keepalives to reduce N on the edge. any logs?

olivia: yep, pulled a snippet from the edge logs: 
```
[edge-ptx] 2025-01-12T10:02:01Z INFO keepalive_sent tenant=acme session=shard-27 coalesced_count=3
[proxy->backend] 2025-01-12T10:02:03Z WARN delayed_ping session=shard-27 last_activity=15s
[backend] 2025-01-12T10:02:05Z INFO stream_closed session=shard-27 reason=idle_timeout
```
Client kept sending tokens but backend considered it idle because our ping ended up arriving after the idle timer window.

sara: that log timestamp delta looks like buffering on the proxy. did we just roll the new keepalive aggregator?

ops-bot: deploy:edge-proxy v3.14.0 -> rolled 09:50 UTC (canary -> 2 regions).

kai: yes, v3.14.0 added coalescing for keepalives if sessions are low-QPS. assumption was safe but apparently interacts badly with streaming idle heuristics.

ryan: rough proposal: do not coalesce keepalives for sessions with an open SSE/WS stream that has seen recent outgoing data OR mark coalesced pings with X-Stream-KA header so backend can extend the idle window. which is less invasive?

olivia: header approach is lower-risk (no change to aggregator) but backend idle timers are in multiple services — would need fast roll across infra. could add a shim in the routing layer to tag them for now.

kai: alternative: change aggregator to respect stream_active boolean — cheap: if stream_active -> pass through immediately, else batch. downside: needs reliable stream_active signal at proxy.

sara: we already annotate sessions with activity flags in the lease metadata. should be straightforward to consult it before coalescing. also need metrics: count of coalesced pings affecting active streams.

ryan: agree on telemetry. console asks: add a dashboard tile showing coalesced_keepalive_vs_resume_failures by region/tenant. current dashboard shows only total resume failures so correlation is buried.

olivia: pulled a quick query for failure spike — linking in thread: https://console.redwood/streams?q=resume_failures%20%7C%20when%20%7B%20timestamp%20%3E%20now()-1h%20%7D

kai: timeline: rollback windows? we need a mitig ASAP. I can push a canary patch to aggregator to skip coalescing when stream_active=true. target 30m.

sara: +1. also add a temporary alert: if coalesced_keepalive_count_for_active_sessions > 5/min fire P3.

ryan: and add a small probe to the client-side SDK to surface reconnect reason tag so product teams see if it was client-initiated or server idle. can we plumb that into logs?

migrations-bot: migration task created: MIG-3482 "skip-ka-coalesce-for-active-streams" assigned to kai, due 2025-01-12T11:00Z.

olivia: for the postmortem: we should list why idle_timeouts are aggressive — backends have 10s idle window to avoid resource leakage. maybe relax to 15s for streams with resume tokens? tradeoff is resource hold time.

kai: let's do the quick fix first (no coalesce on active streams). I'll also add a feature flag so we can toggle per-region without code rollback.

sara: I'll create the dashboard tile and alert. putting a note in the rollout doc to watch resume_failure rate and per-tenant cost.

ryan: long term: consider server-initiated keepalive negotiation — client/server agree on ping cadence and aggregator respects it. avoids surprises.

olivia: thanks all. I'll watch the canary and post updates. if we see < 1% reconnects after patch we can promote. :thumbsup:

kai: starting canary now. will post link to trace IDs.

olivia: (after 10:40) canary looks clean in us-east-1 — coalesced_keepalive_for_active went to 0 and resume_failures dropped by ~92% on the canary shard. promoting to eu-west next.

sara: added dashboard panel: "keepalive coalesce impact" + alert. saved to team dash: https://console.redwood/d/eng-platform/keepalive-impact

ryan: filing follow-ups: change idle timer for resume-capable sessions (PM/eng tradeoff), and client SDK reconnect_reason propagation.

ops-bot: deploy:edge-proxy v3.14.0+patch-1 -> rolled 10:55 UTC (canary->all us-east-1).

olivia: excellent. closing thread once eu-west done. great cross-team response. :party_parrot:
